the elution profiles of nucleic acid from Azotobacter cells change during germination.

nucleic acids of dormant cysts of Azotobacher vinelandii were found to be in a more tightly packed configuration than those of germinated cysts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the nucleic acids of the Azotobacter species.
the isolation of Azotobacters, the study of their physiology and the elucidation of the mechanism of their germination.
the study of the nucleic acid content of dormant Azotobacter and of germinated cysts, and the effect of germination on the nucleic acid composition of the cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the changes in nucleic acids during germination of Azotobacters are not only due to the changes in the nucleic acid composition but also due to changes in the nucleotide configuration.
the elution profiles of nucleic acids are changed during cyst germination, that the elution patterns are not the same for the dormant and the germinated cysts.

Azotobacter can be considered as a model system for the study of nucleic acid fractionation during dormancy, germination, and vegetative growth.

the nucleic acids from Azotobacter cells are not as stable as previously believed.
